---

### Summary

The **tab management workflow** (tab-list, tab-new, tab-select, tab-close) is well-designed and reliable. Commands are named intuitively, output is clear, and the indexed-based + GUID-based dual targeting system is a good design choice. The snapshot verification pattern works well for confirming context after tab switches.

However, the **first-time experience is significantly marred** by the PowerShell wrapper issues. A user following the documented workflow (`goto → snapshot -v 0 → click`) would encounter confusing failures on step 2, and the documented `--` separator workaround doesn't work. This is the single biggest barrier to a smooth onboarding experience.

The noise level is also higher than it should be: cargo build warnings on every invocation and the b4w.sh nag message create a sense that something is wrong even when everything is working fine.

issues.title: PowerShell -v flag interception makes snapshot -v 0 fail with b4w.ps1

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 snapshot -v 0

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Snapshot captured with viewport 0 (top of page).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Error: Unknown command: 'snapshot-0'. Did you mean: 'snapshot'? The -v flag was consumed by PowerShell as -Verbose, leaving '0' appended to 'snapshot'.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: PowerShell's parameter binder matches -v to its built-in -Verbose common parameter before the script's $RemainingArgs collection receives it. The script uses [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)] which only collects arguments not matched by any declared parameter, but -v matches -Verbose.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.ps1: the param() block and how RemainingArgs is forwarded to cargo run

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a -v shorthand param to b4w.ps1 that explicitly passes it through to the CLI (e.g., [switch]$v plus manual argument reconstruction)
- Or document prominently that Linux/bash users should prefer b4w.sh, and explain why
- Fix the documented -- separator workaround (currently broken: 'Parameter name '' is ambiguous')
- Consider detecting pwsh version and warning about known parameter binding conflicts

issues.title: Documented -- separator workaround for b4w.ps1 doesn't work

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -- snapshot -v 0

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The -- separator should pass snapshot -v 0 through to the CLI.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: PowerShell error: 'Parameter cannot be processed because the parameter name '' is ambiguous. Possible matches include: -Rebuild -RemainingArgs -Verbose ...'

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The b4w.ps1 param block declares [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)] which doesn't interact correctly with -- when the script itself is the target. PowerShell's -- separator only works for native commands, not script parameters.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.ps1: param() declaration and argument forwarding logic

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Either fix b4w.ps1 to properly handle -- separator by parsing it before the param block
- Or update the SKILL.md documentation to remove this as a recommended workaround since it doesn't work
- Or recommend using b4w.sh on Linux/macOS and b4w.bat on Windows CMD as the primary workaround

issues.title: b4w.sh prints intrusive nag message on every invocation

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run any command via ./b4w.sh. E.g., ./b4w.sh tab-list

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Clean output with only the command result, or at most a one-time warning.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every invocation prints: 'It is strongly recommended to launch pwsh and run the .ps1 commands directly within the pwsh terminal.' This appears on stderr for every single command, creating noise.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: b4w.sh includes this warning unconditionally before every execution, likely as a cross-platform guidance mechanism, but it fires on every command rather than once per session.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.sh: the echo/warning line before the pwsh invocation

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Only print the warning once per shell session (e.g., check for an env var like B4W_SH_WARNED)
- Or remove the warning entirely on Linux since pwsh is an optional dependency, not the native shell
- Or move the warning to stderr with a --quiet guard so --json consumers aren't affected

issues.title: Help output is a wall of text — category filters are buried at the bottom

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 help or ./b4w.ps1 --help

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Concise overview with clear pointers to drill down. Category filters should be prominent.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The help output lists every command in a large flat wall. The category filter hint ('Filter help by category: --help nav | --help extract | ...') appears as a single line near the top but is easily missed. A first-time user sees ~200 lines of commands with no obvious structure.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The help system prioritizes completeness over discoverability. All commands are shown at once rather than using a hierarchical drill-down approach.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (help/usage formatting module)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Default help should show only top-level categories with a prominent 'Use --help <category> for details' message
- Add a 'Getting Started' section at the very top with the 3 most common commands (goto, snapshot, click)
- Use color or bold to visually distinguish category headers from individual commands
- Consider an interactive --help that asks what you want to do (navigate, extract, etc.)

issues.title: Cargo build warning clutters every command output

sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Demote the skill-file embedding message from warning to info/message level
- Or redirect cargo stderr in b4w.sh/b4w.ps1 and only show it when the build actually fails
- Consider embedding skill files only during release builds, not dev builds

issues.title: tab-new auto-switches to the new tab with no opt-out

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Open multiple tabs: tab-new url1, then tab-new url2

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Option to open tab in background (stay on current tab) or foreground (switch to new tab).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: tab-new always switches to the new tab. To open multiple tabs and stay on the original, you must tab-select back after each tab-new.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: tab-new always calls tab-select after creating the tab. There's no --background flag.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (tab-new handler), and the backend MCP tool that creates tabs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a --background flag to tab-new that creates the tab without switching to it
- Document the auto-switch behavior more prominently (it's mentioned but buried in the examples section notes)

issues.title: No tab-title or tab-url command for quick context checks

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: After switching tabs, you need to run a full snapshot just to verify which page you're on.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A lightweight command like 'tab-current' or 'tab-info' that shows the current tab's URL and title without a full snapshot.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The only way to confirm the current page is to run 'snapshot' or 'tab-list' and infer which tab is active. Snapshot takes a full accessibility tree capture which is overkill for a simple context check.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: No lightweight tab-state query command exists. tab-list shows all tabs but doesn't highlight the active one.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a 'tab-current' command that prints just the active tab's index, GUID, title, and URL
- Or add an active-tab indicator (e.g., '*') in the tab-list output to show which tab has focus
- This would reduce the need for full snapshots during tab-switching workflows

issues.title: tab-list doesn't indicate which tab is currently active

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Open 3 tabs, switch to tab 1, then run tab-list

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The currently active tab should be visually marked (e.g., with an asterisk or arrow).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: tab-list shows all tabs identically. After switching tabs multiple times, the user has no way to tell from tab-list output which tab is active without running a snapshot.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The tab-list output format doesn't include an active-tab indicator despite having access to this information from the browser.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: Backend: the tab-list handler in the session/tab management code

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a '*' or '>' prefix to the active tab row in tab-list output
- Include an 'active' boolean field in the --json output for tab-list
- Document which tab becomes active after tab-close (currently unspecified)
